exposure: Lower glycemic criteria for diagnosis of gestational diabetes (fasting >=92 mg/dL, 1-hour >=180 mg/dL, or 2-hour >=153 mg/dL)
Higher glycemic criteria for diagnosis of gestational diabetes (fasting >=99 mg/dL or 2-hour >=162 mg/dL)
outcome: Large for gestational age infant (birth weight above 90th percentile)
Maternal and infant health (e.g., induction of labor, use of health services, use of pharmacologic agents, neonatal hypoglycemia)
cohort: Pregnant women (n=4061) at 24 to 32 weeks' gestation were randomly assigned to be evaluated for gestational diabetes using either lower or higher glycemic criteria.
finding: The use of lower glycemic criteria for diagnosing gestational diabetes did not result in a lower risk of large-for-gestational-age infants compared to higher glycemic criteria.
birth_weight: Large for gestational age (defined as a birth weight above the 90th percentile according to Fenton. World Health Organization standards)
gest_age: Women at 24 to 32 weeks' gestation; outcome defined by 'large for gestational age' based on gestational age at birth
